one_month_reasoning: In the window: Q3 FY2027 results (quarter ended 2026-10-31), not yet dated, expected around 2026-11-18 to 11-25 (last year 2025-11-19), with the Q4 outlook and first FY28 colour. Q3 guide revenue $1.90-1.98B, adj EPS $4.33-4.79; Street 4.33; whisper 4.55 (80% 4.24-4.86); our model 5.22. DY has beaten its EPS guide by 13-62% three quarters running, but the industry read-through is mixed-to-negative for the outlook: MasTec's Communications revenue fell 11.8% with backlog -7.5% q/q and customer deferrals in H2 2026, and AT&T cut its 2027-28 capital-investment outlook. Past print reactions were huge in both directions (May 2026 +24% week, Aug 2026 -25% week). The stock is -61% from its high with a sector-wide de-rating (MTZ -56%, FIX -42% from highs), so reversal and continued momentum roughly cancel. I centre the distribution at today's price with a monthly sigma of ~19% (annual 53%/3.5 = 15% widened for the print), no directional tilt.

downside.story: 10th percentile: the carrier pause MasTec describes spreads to DY's top customers: AT&T and Verizon cut 2027 fiber/wireless programs (NTM backlog -12% vs base, book-to-bill under 1), Communications margin -200bp as crews are under-absorbed (MasTec's comms margin fell 460bp y/y), data-center electrical work slips (BS share -25%: third-party data-center delays, labor), and the P/E de-rates 3 turns to ~10x (LMB/STRL trough levels).

base.story: Median: carriers keep fiber builds going at a slower pace (AT&T to 60M locations by 2030 via its own capex and the GIP/CPP JV; Verizon toward 40-50M), deferred wireless returns in FY28, BEAD construction starts, long-haul builds for hyperscalers add volume; DY's NTM backlog grows ~7%/yr in FY28 (below the approved +10%), margins edge up, data-center electrical tracks the Census market at a fading share; the stock re-rates only part of the way (13.2x NTM).

upside.story: 90th percentile: deferred wireless (~$150M) and BEAD construction land in FY28 together with hyperscaler long-haul awards (Lumen PCF, MasTec-like 2,000+ mile programs), NTM backlog +8% vs base, margin +100bp on volume leverage, Building Systems share +15% as hyperscalers guide 2027 capex up, and the multiple recovers 3 turns toward the peer median (16x).

sbc_treatment.note: Adjusted EPS basis excludes only amortization; SBC (0.53% of revenue) is deducted in corporate_ebit, so sbc_pct_rev is 0 and the share count falls only by net buybacks (-0.5%/yr). Peers' consensus EPS bases differ slightly (most adjusted EPS also include SBC).

reasoning: Industry lane. 1) Why the stock halved: the de-rating is sector-wide (MTZ -56%, FIX -42%, EME -28% from 52-week highs per Twelve Data quotes) and, for DY, the Aug 26 guide (wireless ~$150M deferred to FY28, comms margin slight decline) plus a new low on Oct 20-21, the same day AT&T lowered its long-term capital-investment outlook ($22-23B a year in 2027-28 vs $23-24B in 2026) and a week before MasTec showed Communications revenue -11.8%, margin 6.7%, 18-month backlog -7.5% q/q, with customers deferring H2 2026 spend. Peers with data-center exposure fell on strong prints (FIX book-to-bill ~2), so sentiment ('AI build-out ends next year') is part of it. 2) Chain view of demand: carriers - AT&T still targets 60M fiber locations by 2030 (39M now) partly via a GIP/CPP JV, signed multiyear fiber supply with Corning, and Verizon targets 40-50M passings (32M at YE26) while cutting opex and capex slightly; long-haul - Lumen plans 30M new intercity fiber miles by 2028 and MasTec won 2,100 hyperscaler miles for mid-2027; BEAD - ~$21B after savings, ~63% fiber, construction peaks 2027-2030; data centers - Census put-in-place at a record $96.5B SAAR, hyperscalers guide 2027 capex up, but Microsoft cited third-party data-center delays. Net: volume keeps growing but slower than the approved backlog path, so I cut comms_ntm_backlog growth to ~7%/yr FY28 and ~6% FY29 (worth about -$9/share) and keep the other approved drivers. 3) Valuation: model EPS FY27 ~18.3 (Zacks 15.98, SA 17.06: +7-15%, mostly the beat record already in H1 and Q3 at 5.22 vs whisper 4.55), FY28 ~19.8 (Zacks 18.98 +4%, SA 20.77 -5%), FY29 ~22.4 (Zacks 22.37, in line). Horizon P/E 13.2x from the shrink rule (k=0.8) on a 4-name whole-company peer median of 18.65x; EV/EBITDA 10.9x cross-check. 4) Scenarios move backlog, comms margin and BS share plus the multiple; the downside sits further from base (fat left tail) because customer concentration (AT&T + Verizon 30.5%) and an industry deferral are the visible risks. Research was limited to web search/fetch; X/social sources not used. sec.gov filings were read with WebFetch; no request carried a name or email.

Actual through Sep 2026 (U.S. Census Bureau, Value of Private Construction Put in Place, SAAR, "Data center" column (https://www.census.gov/construction/c30/xlsx/privsatime.xlsx; September 2026 release CB26-176, 2026-11-02): Sep-26p $96,462M, Aug-26r $88,815M, Sep-25 $50,700M; CY2024 avg $34,718M, CY2025 $49,712M); Oct 2026-Jan 2027 held at the Sep-26 level (flag); CY2027 = CY2026 x 1,070/800 = 103,357, CY2028 x 1,300/1,070 = 125,574 (Hyperscaler capex consensus path (adhoc/nvda_customer_capex.md, as of 2026-10-05, [secondary]): Goldman Sachs 2026-09-24 top-5 consensus $800B (2026) -> $1,070B (2027) -> ~$1,300B (2028)), CY2029 +10% = 138,131 (estimate: growth fades; variant flat); months log-linear from Sep-26 through each year's mid-point, rescaled to the CY totals. dep_rate 2.75% of revenue (depreciation ex amortization: Q1 FY27 53.3/1,964.8 = 2.72%, Q2 55.2/2,005.9 = 2.75%; XBRL D&A less AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets). sbc_rate 0.53% (SBC Q1 10.6, Q2 10.3). other_addback 2.5 (Q1 FY27 3.5, Q2 2.4; see ebit_basis_note).

horizon_multiples.peer_basis: whole-company peers with >=25% fit (MTZ 16.6x, PWR 35.2x, PRIM 17.1x, MYRG 20.2x NTM; median 18.65x); DY own NTM 12.1x on Zacks time-weighted NTM EPS 18.23; exit = 18.65 x (12.1/18.65)^0.8 = 13.2x
trailing GAAP EV/EBITDA of PRIM 14.5x and MYRG 13.2x (peers.md; median 13.85x); DY own ~9.9x; k = 0.71 (tested for trailing EV/EBITDA): 13.85 x (9.9/13.85)^0.71 = 10.9x

downside.story: 10th percentile: the carrier pause MasTec describes spreads to DY's top customers: AT&T and Verizon cut 2027 fiber/wireless programs (NTM backlog -12% vs base, book-to-bill under 1), Communications margin -200bp as crews are under-absorbed (MasTec's comms margin fell 460bp y/y), data-center electrical work slips (BS share -25%: third-party data-center delays, labor), and the P/E de-rates 3 turns to ~10x (LMB/STRL trough levels).

upside.story: 90th percentile: deferred wireless (~$150M) and BEAD construction land in FY28 together with hyperscaler long-haul awards (Lumen PCF, MasTec-like 2,000+ mile programs), NTM backlog +8% vs base, margin +100bp on volume leverage, Building Systems share +15% as hyperscalers guide 2027 capex up, and the multiple recovers 3 turns toward the peer median (16x).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set built on the approved DY set (drivers, quarters, driver_build, years.shareholder_returns as approved) with ONE deliberate difference: agent_2's comms_ntm_backlog path is lower (industry evidence, see the driver derivation); all other driver values are the approved ones. Value is carried by the P/E (ntm) leg (0.75) on the build's own EPS (adjusted EBIT = GAAP operating income + amortization, SBC costed in corporate_ebit, so sbc_pct_rev = 0 to avoid double counting) and a trailing EV/EBITDA cross-check (0.25) on engine EBITDA (~GAAP EBITDA). No DCF (policy). No SOTP: both segments are contracting businesses valued on the same earnings multiple; a BS-only peer median (EME 18.5x, FIX 19.1x, STRL 13.9x, LMB 10.0x; 16.2x) is close to the whole-company peer median, so a split adds little. Weights are judgment.
model_inputs.gap_note: 1) Supplier finance program: a prior round reported $367.4M (10-Q note 22); I could not confirm it in the part of the 10-Q I read (accounts payable rose from $497.3M to $610.0M between 2026-01-31 and 2026-08-01 [1]), so no debt-like adjustment is in the set; treating $367.4M as debt would cut ~$12/share. 2) Backlog path below the approved drivers (about -$9/share vs the approved path at the same multiples): judgment call for Kilian. 3) EV/EBITDA leg uses only two telecom-fit peers with trailing figures (PRIM, MYRG). 4) Next print Q3 FY27 not yet dated (last year 2025-11-19). 5) No financing event >=20% probability found; net debt/EBITDA ~2.3x and falls with FCF.
